name: Langflow
tagline: Build AI applications with visual workflows and Python components.
hook: A full-stack guide to dependencies, authorization boundaries, saved-flow class names, components, environments, and tests.
summary: Langflow maps its Python backend, frontend, and component system. It explains dependency direction, distinguishes an authorization interface from the plugin that enforces it, and protects class names stored in saved flows. Each package has its own environment and tests.

techniques.title: Make dependency direction explicit
techniques.body: The package chain gives an agent a way to judge where new imports and provider integrations belong. Architecture is described as a dependency constraint, beyond a directory listing.

techniques.title: Distinguish a switch from enforcement
techniques.body: The authorization notes explain that enabling the interface alone does not introduce a deny policy. An agent changing permission-sensitive behavior must account for the registered implementation.
techniques.quote: When enabled with only the OSS stub registered, every check returns allow — the stub is a no-op so routes stay wired and audit rows still flow. Real allow/deny requires a registered authorization plugin.

techniques.title: Protect identifiers stored in user data
techniques.body: Class names are part of saved-flow compatibility. A rename that looks local in Python can break existing documents, so the instruction calls it out as a persistent contract.
techniques.quote: Changing a component's class name is a breaking change and should never be done. The class name serves as an identifier used to match components in saved flows and to flag them for updates in the UI. Renaming it will break existing flows that use that component.

techniques.title: Include the subpackage development environment
techniques.body: The test setup names the package whose development dependencies must be synchronized. A root install is not evidence that component test dependencies are present.

steal: Write the allowed dependency direction as an explicit chain.
Document when a feature flag enables an interface without enforcing a policy.
Identify code names that are serialized into user data.
Include package-specific dependency setup beside test commands.
